## Purpose and entry points
Graphify is a Python 3.10+ local-first CLI that maps source code and other project artifacts into a queryable knowledge graph. Main invocation routes are the package module entry point and CLI dispatcher: `graphify/__main__.py`, `graphify/cli.py`. It produces `graphify-out/graph.json`, an HTML visualization, and a Markdown report; it also exposes query, path, explain, update, export, install, and serving commands.

## Extraction pipeline
`graphify/extract.py` orchestrates corpus walking, ignore handling, parallel extraction, cache reuse, incremental updates, and safety checks against incomplete/shrunk graphs. Code extraction is deterministic AST parsing through the extractor registry and engine: `graphify/extractors/__init__.py`, `graphify/extractors/engine.py`, `graphify/extractors/models.py`. Language-specific extractors emit a shared node/edge model; cross-file symbol and import/call resolution occur after syntax extraction.

## Graph construction and normalization
Raw per-file results are merged into the canonical graph by `graphify/build.py`, with stable identities supplied by `graphify/ids.py`. This is the central boundary between extraction output and persisted/queryable graph topology. Build-time cleanup includes duplicate-entity reconciliation and semantic hygiene: `graphify/dedup.py`, `graphify/semantic_cleanup.py`; it must preserve/remap relationships, including multigraph/hyperedge-compatible structures in `graphify/multigraph_compat.py`.

## Resolution, confidence, and enrichment
Resolver layers turn syntactic references into cross-file relationships while preserving whether an edge was directly observed or inferred. Key dispatch points are `graphify/resolver_registry.py`, `graphify/symbol_resolution.py`, and `graphify/extractors/resolution.py`. Additional ingestion enriches the same graph from package manifests, MCP configurations, SCIP, PostgreSQL, Cargo, Google Workspace, and external repositories: `graphify/manifest_ingest.py`, `graphify/mcp_ingest.py`, `graphify/scip_ingest.py`.

## Analysis and outputs
Post-build analysis identifies connected hubs, communities, and reportable structure: `graphify/analyze.py`, `graphify/cluster.py`, `graphify/report.py`. Exporters serialize the graph to interactive HTML and graph databases: `graphify/export.py`, `graphify/exporters/html.py`, `graphify/exporters/graphdb.py`. Alternative derived views include wiki/tree/call-flow artifacts in `graphify/wiki.py` and `graphify/callflow_html.py`.

## Query, automation, and service boundaries
Local graph consumers use `graphify/querylog.py`, `graphify/affected.py`, and CLI query/path/explain operations. `graphify/serve.py` provides MCP over stdio or HTTP, optionally API-key-protected, making graph queries available to IDE agents or shared deployments. `graphify/install.py` and `graphify/hooks.py` integrate graph-first instructions and update hooks into multiple AI assistants; generated skill content is sourced from `tools/skillgen/`.

## Runtimes and external services
The core runtime is Python with tree-sitter-based local code parsing. Optional semantic/document extraction routes through configurable LLM backends represented by `graphify/llm.py`, including OpenAI-compatible APIs, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Ollama, and Claude CLI. Optional infrastructure targets include Docker (`Dockerfile`), Neo4j/FalkorDB graph export, PostgreSQL introspection (`graphify/pg_introspect.py`), Google Workspace (`graphify/google_workspace.py`), and GitHub PR metadata (`graphify/prs.py`).
